KorrAI started in 2021 as a spin-off from a Canadian Space Agency research project. We spent four years building ground motion monitoring for mines and infrastructure, and kept running into the same problem. The engineers who sign off on a site's safety work from decades of reports, sensor readings, and surveys held by consultants, contractors, and site teams, and they assemble that record by hand.

TRAIL is our AI platform for those decisions. Mining is our focus, starting with mine closure, where legacy sites carry decades of fragmented records, and a wrong answer has regulatory and safety consequences. We are a 20-person team of geoscientists and AI engineers, and we monitor more than $100 billion in assets across 5 million sq. km.

Who we serve:

TRAIL is used by the people who manage risk on critical infrastructure. In mining, that means closure professionals, geotechnical engineers, and Engineers of Record at mining companies, engineering consultancies, and regulators. For data centers and other critical infrastructure, risk engineers and underwriters use TRAIL for site selection, feasibility, and construction risk. 

We have worked with organizations including Agnico Eagle, Hecla, Eldorado Gold Corporation, Stantec, AECOM, Ramboll, Amazon Web Services and Zurich North America.
long_description.after:
KorrAI began in 2021 as a Canadian Space Agency research spin-off. We spent four years on ground deformation monitoring and geotechnical studies for mines and infrastructure, and kept running into the same problem: engineers who sign off on a site's safety have to synthesize reports by hunting for docs and data received from consultants, contractors, and site teams by hand.

Over the last two years, we built TRAIL, a platform informed by interconnected data, powered by specialised AI agents, and supported by our experts. With TRAIL deployed at multiple mine sites across the US and Canada, we envision turning risk management into a proactive process. When records span decades, a wrong answer has regulatory and safety consequences; it is necessary to have complete knowledge of risks and take action in time. 

Our team of satellite data experts, geoscientists, and AI engineers monitors more than $100 billion in assets across the globe. TRAIL reads a site's full record: reports, drawings, inspection notes, monitoring data, satellite imagery, and ground deformation, etc. It builds a location-based knowledge graph. AI Agents run defined risk passes over the graph, flag contradictions, cross-link data, and present findings. Every finding cites its source page and data point, so a regulator or Engineer of Record can review it. Where no evidence supports a claim, TRAIL says so.

TRAIL is used by closure professionals, geotechnical engineers, and Engineers of Record in mining, and by risk engineers and underwriters on data centers and other critical infrastructure. We work with organizations including Agnico Eagle, Hecla, Eldorado Gold, Stantec, AECOM, Ramboll, Amazon Web Services, and Zurich North America.

long_description.before:
Email sucks. It takes forever to go through, and hiring an assistant is costly and invasive. Friday is building the assistant that learns how to predict the action that you will take on your emails, and does it for you.

Today's email products try to help you go through your emails a little faster, but if you have to get through 1000 emails, those products doesn't do much for you. 

The reality is, most of the emails you get don't require you to personally look at them. Freestyle completely eliminates the need to check those emails, and handles them all at once for you, immediately. 

Freestyle is here to file away spam, sift through newsletters for important tidbits, text you important notifications, and reply to mundane emails, so that no matter how many thousands of emails are in your inbox, you'll just be left with the few emails that actually require your personal touch.

Getting this right is difficult, so everyone else settles with trying to help you go through your email twice as fast. If you want to go 100x as fast, you shouldn't spend even a second on useless emails. 

Freestyle gets this right, bringing the elite experience of having a professional assistant to the entire world.

long_description.before:
Conntour enables government agencies to query their video - from security cameras, body cams, and drones.

Users can search past footage (“Find a man with tattoos on his left arm”), configure real-time alerts (“Notify me if someone climbs over the wall”), and extract data (“How many pickup trucks entered yesterday?”).

Unlike traditional video analytics solutions, which are limited to fixed parameters (like a weapon, bag, or car color), Conntour supports an unlimited range of highly specific scenarios described in plain language. This enables a single human to monitor thousands of cameras, or find a specific moment in minutes instead of days.

What makes Conntour's technology unique is its ability to process video using natural language at scale, fully on-premises, with minimal hardware requirements. The system is already deployed with mission-critical teams at leading intelligence and homeland security agencies.

Conntour is backed by top-tier investors including General Catalyst and Y Combinator, was selected for the first-ever Palantir Fellowship, and has the former CTO of the CIA on its advisory board.

long_description.before:
Ruma Care automates all admin work for infusion clinics - starting with prior authorizations & copay assistance enrollment.

Biologics are expensive medications that cost $80-$150K+ per year per patient, and often need to be administered in specific settings called infusion clinics. Medical providers buy these drugs up front to secure pricing deals and safer inventory - they are reimbursed for the cost of the medications through the patients’ insurance. 

Current medical workflows aren't built for infusion clinics. Inventory, storage, transport, and billing is still managed through paper and excel spreadsheets. And because they’re so expensive, these specialty medications are denied by insurers at a rate of 37% each year. When they are denied, when workflows fail, or patients are infused before paperwork is cleared, providers don’t get reimbursed for the medication and are left covering the costs. Ruma Care solves this so clinics get paid, patients get treated faster, and care teams spend less time fighting forms. 

We do this in three ways: 
1. For each medication, diagnosis, and insurance combination, Ruma extracts the submission criteria required to get the drug approved by insurers. 
2. We pull out the correct forms, then automate the form-filling for prior authorizations. 
3. Lastly, we enroll patients in copay assistance programs, all in one workflow and platform. 

We turn a process that traditionally spans 70+ online portals, disparate paper forms, and manual phone calling into a single, streamlined platform. As we process prior authorizations, our models learn from denial patterns to understand exactly what insurers need to see to get a prior authorization approved.
long_description.after:
